newsitem.title: USA: Pittsburgh cop faces lawsuit in fiancee's suicide.
newsitem.headline: Pittsburgh cop faces lawsuit in fiancee's suicide.

text.p: A white police officer who was acquitted last year in the death of a black motorist now faces a lawsuit from the family of his former fiancee alleging that he caused her 1993 suicide by repeatedly abusing her.

The wrongful death lawsuit filed Thursday comes less than a year after John Vojtas, a police sergeant in the Pittsburgh suburb of Brentwood, was acquitted of involuntary manslaughter in the death of Jonny Gammage, who died of asphyxiation while being held face down on the ground in October 1995.
Gammage was in the custody of Vojtas and four other white police officers, who testified that the motorist became violent after a routine traffic stop.

The suit filed by the family of Judith Barrett, who lived with Vojtas and was 26 when she died, alleges that he repeatedly beat her at home and in public and was responsible for her shooting death, which was ruled a suicide.

Barrett was found dead in a bus shelter in June 1993 with a gunshot wound caused by a bullet from Vojtas' gun. The suit says Vojtas and the borough of Brentwood are responsible for damages in excess of $25,000 based on charges of assault, battery, wrongful death and civil rights violations.
The suit seeks damages from Brentwood because it alleges borough officials knew about Vojtas' violent behaviour and did nothing to stop it. Attorneys for Vojtas were not available for comment.
